original_question: Determine whether an ultrapower NU of a II1 factor can ever be isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra.
target_in_paper: Miscellaneous, Problem 39: Is N^U ever isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem almost verbatim: it asks whether a tracial ultrapower N^U of a II1 factor can be isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra.
missing_details: The paper fixes U to be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ℕ.
The notation N^U refers specifically to the tracial ultrapower of N.
The question is existential over all choices of II1 factors N and all nonprincipal ultrafilters U: the paper asks whether this can ever happen at all.
To make the target object fully explicit, one should write it as L(G) for some discrete group G.
The intended isomorphism is an isomorphism of von Neumann algebras (equivalently here, of tracial von Neumann algebras).
The paper does not add extra hypotheses such as separability, amenability, property Gamma, or Connes embeddability, so the refined question should not add them.

The nearby context notes known obstructions: ultrapowers cannot be nontrivial tensor products, crossed products, amalgamated free products, or have diffuse regular abelian subalgebras; this motivates the question but is not part of the formal statement.
refined_question: Do there exist a II1 factor N, a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, and a discrete group G such that the tracial ultrapower N^U is isomorphic, as a von Neumann algebra, to the group von Neumann algebra L(G)?
justification: The draft is aimed directly at the paper’s Problem 39 in the Miscellaneous section. The only paper-defined context needed to make it fully stand-alone is the opening notation fixing U as a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ℕ and N^U as the tracial ultrapower. The sentence immediately after Problem 39 supplies the nearby structural context from Popa’s arguments, but it does not replace Problem 39 with a different or broader formulation. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply the explicit existential version asking for some II1 factor N, some nonprincipal ultrafilter U, and some discrete group G with N^U ≅ L(G).
